campaigns.title: Nourish a Child. Nurture Their Future.
campaigns.description: Every child deserves a healthy start in life.Good nutrition and healthcare are essential for a child's growth, learning and development. Yet, for children growing up in migrant and underserved communities, access to both remains a challenge.In Hyderabad's urban settlements and brick kiln communities, families face difficult living and working conditions, with limited access to nutritious food and basic healthcare. This affects children's health, growth and ability to learn.At Youth Feed Foundation, we believe that a child's circumstances should not determine their opportunity to grow, learn and thrive.What Your Contribution SupportsYour donation will support two Youth Feed Foundation programmes:Project Gyan Shakthi: Supporting children attending community learning centres.Project Brick Kiln: Supporting young children and adolescents living in migrant brick kiln communities.Through these programmes, we provide:This Children's Day, Help Us Reach More ChildrenThanks to our matching restaurant partners from NRAI Hyderabad, every contribution will be matched, strengthening the nutrition and healthcare support provided to each child.Every contribution, big or small, helps us reach more children with the nutrition and healthcare they need.Support a child today. Help us reach 1,500 children.#YFFChildrensDay2026Please note: WE ACCEPT ONLY INDIAN DONATIONSAs per Foreign Contribution Regulation Act 2010, we cannot accept donations from Foreign Citizens, OCI/PIO card holders, or Indian citizens residing outside India. Please donate only if you do not fall in these categories.

campaigns.title: Runway of Hope 2026 | Support India's Government Schools
campaigns.description: A child enters the school halls with open eyes, ears, and heart. Learning every day. Learning how to say hi, be friends, and help each other.Learning ABC, 1+1, and what keeps plants alive? (Hint: it’s the sun)Learning how to dream:I want to become the president and give shelter to people who sleep on streetsI want to be a gamer and make my parents proudI will be a teacher and teach children who can’t afford schoolBut here’s what happens. Many fail to gain foundational learning skills; they can’t read or comprehend sentences, or even do simple 2-digit subtraction by age 8. Only 30% of them go on to pursue higher education. These children could have been the next big scientist, researcher, or director of India. But they fall victim to an unequal education system that makes circumstances matter more than their potential. Today, 140 million children in India study in primary Government schools.  There are children in these schools with dreams, but at the risk of losing their shot at a prosperous, thriving future. There is one way we can save millions of futures: teachersOne great teacher can shift a student's academic trajectory.But India’s teachers are crushed under a wide range of responsibilities and little support. Teachers carry the state’s aspirations for a high-quality education system, but do not receive the support and systems that can enable them. In 2025, NCERT (PARAKH) reported that only 35% of teachers in India received any professional development.Teachers are bent over backward trying to do their best and always looking for ways to do more:It was a dream to see my class read a book. For years I wasn't able to do it. Today 60% of them can.My grade 3 children used to feel so underconfident in English; it wasn’t just about ability, but just this hesitation. Today, they can read English paragraphs, and they are more confident and outspokenI used to focus on what children couldn’t do, but never really thought about where I could get better, and what I needed to change. I am starting to reflect and do that nowThat is the work. Teachers learning, re-learning & trying. At SEF, we work with the one person in that classroom who can change what happens next.6 programs across 3 states, building the training, coaching, and classroom resources that teachers were always supposed to have.90% relevance score for our trainings and 2x learning outcomes Today, we work with 2 lakh current and future teachers and 3M children.By 2030, we will work with one million. That's millions more children with a chance of a better future.That is the runway we are building. Every teacher on it is carrying a room full of children who still believe they are going to be president, or a gamer, or the teacher who comes back for the kids who can't pay.By donating, you are not just funding one teacher or one classroom. You are funding every classroom those 2 lakh teachers will ever walk into, and every child who has a dream.The future is in their hands.

campaigns.title: It isn't easy to sleep on an empty stomach, is it?
campaigns.description: I Chetna Shah, celebrating my Birthday month, would want nothing more than a celebration that leaves an impact on someone's life, and hence have decided to celebrate it with Project Smilestones.In all these years, my most truthful and satisfying experience has been all my seva efforts towards Shrimad Rajchandra Aatma Tatva Research Centre.Shrimad Rajchandra Aatma Tatva Research Centre is a non-profit organization driving a lot of major projects for society. One of them is hunger alleviation.We forget how lucky we are and take for granted all the hot, fresh, healthy food served to us all day, every day! As a small step toward a larger cause, I’ve initiated a fundraiser to help get one meal to the table of these 650+ beneficiaries children and their families.I have personally volunteered and seen the conditions people live in and the joy and desperation this lunch meal means to them. Among all the other initiatives the NGO works towards, this one is by far the closest to my heart.But no good impact, big or small, can be made without the support of your own tribe. I am therefore looking for your support and contribution. Please back my fundraiser, so together we can build a better India and a brighter future for all the generations that lie ahead!If you see merit in this, please contribute any amount you like. Remember, no amount is big or small! You will get an 80G certificate and tax exemption for your donation. Loads of love and blessings to you!

campaigns.title: Help abandoned elderly with shelter and care
campaigns.description: 1 in 4 elders in urban India is abused by their own son or daughter-in-law.Every day, elderly parents are left alone on streets, at railway stations, even outside temples. Many are sick, have little money and struggle with age-related illnesses. Often it takes weeks or months before the painful truth comes out: they were abandoned by their own families.Indian law makes it mandatory for children and relatives to care for senior citizens. Yet elder abuse and abandonment continue to rise.Why are elders being abandoned?Changing families: The joint family once had room for elders, cared for across generations. With rapid urbanisation and nuclear families, many elders are now isolated, neglected or abandoned.Poverty and poor healthcare: Small pensions and limited healthcare leave elders dependent on their families. As their health declines and costs rise, many face abuse and abandonment, especially women and widows.How our NGO partners help Our NGO partners work on the ground to rescue abandoned elders and give them shelter, care and dignity. Through old age homes across India, these seniors get to live their golden years in peace, comfort and security, surrounded by compassion.Your donation will help:Fund rescue operations to bring more elders off the streetsProvide shelter, food, healthcare, love and respectGive elders the peace of living among their peersMeet Sulochana At 70, no longer “useful” to her family, Sulochana was taken to Chennai and abandoned at a bus stand. She survived on odd jobs for six years until well-wishers brought her to our NGO partner Akshaya Trust. A medical checkup found a hearing disability, which was treated. Today, she has spent two happy years at Akshaya Trust, where she’s known for her kind heart and warm friendships with other residents.No elder should spend their final years alone. Donate today and give an abandoned senior safety, care and hope.

campaigns.title: Help Disabled Children with Shelter & Care
campaigns.description: Over 20% of the world’s blind people live in India.India has an estimated 4.95 million blind people and 70 million people with vision impairment, including around 2.4 lakh blind children. Disability and poverty often go hand in hand, and for visually impaired children the struggle is even harder. Many face cruel stigma in their own homes and are pushed into isolation.What disabled children faceStigma and misconceptions: Many disabled children are abandoned at birth or face a lifelong struggle. Blindness is often seen as a tragedy, and many believe the disabled can’t study, work or care for themselves. With the right training and tools, they can do nearly everything sighted people can.A struggle for the basics: “How will a disabled person work?” This question keeps talented people out of jobs. Even educated candidates face silent rejection, not because they can’t perform, but because employers won’t include them.How our NGO partners help Our NGO partners give blind and disabled children and young adults shelter, care and education, equipping those overlooked by their families and society with the skills to build a better life.Your donation will help:Fund the rescue of blind and disabled children abandoned by their ownProvide shelter, food, healthcare and educationEquip blind children and young adults with skills for a bright futureMeet Rani Rani, from a small village in Bihar’s Champaran district, lost her eyesight at just four. Years of discrimination followed, but she never gave up on her dream of an education. Seeing her determination, the National Association for the Blind, Delhi supported her higher studies. Today Rani is pursuing her graduation at Miranda House, Delhi, balancing academics and co-curriculars. “If you have the will, you can achieve anything,” she says.Donate today and help a blind or disabled child build the future they deserve.

Every referral we pass and every relationship we build grows from a simple belief that when we lift others, we rise together.Today, I invite you to carry that principle beyond business and into the life of a child.Right now, children are waiting for heart surgeries, while parents pray every day to see their children start school, celebrate birthdays and grow into their dreams.For these families, timely medical care is not a luxury. It is a new lease of life.WHY NOEL FOUNDATION?Since 2013, Noel Foundation has worked to transform the lives of children and families through three focused missions:01 | LIFE-SAVING MISSION: Giving children a second chance at life.Through our Save A Child's Heart initiative, we support children who need life-saving heart surgeries, medical interventions and post-operative care.02 | LIFE-ENHANCING MISSION: Opening doors to education and opportunity.Through educational assistance, learning initiatives and skill development, we help children and young people overcome barriers and build promising futures.03 | LIFE-CARING MISSION: Standing beside children and families.Through counselling, rehabilitation assistance, family support and initiatives such as The Haven, we ensure families are not left to face life's challenges alone.OUR FUNDRAISING GOALWe aim to raise ₹5,00,000 to support children and families who urgently need help.Every contribution counts, whether it is Rs.500, Rs.1,000, Rs.5,000 or more. Together, small acts of generosity can create a life-changing impact.You may never meet the child whose life you help save. But your kindness could be the reason a family smiles again and a little heart gets another chance to beat.BUSINESS BUILDS SUCCESS. GIVING BUILDS HUMANITY.I personally invite each of you to join me in this meaningful cause. Please contribute today and help give a little heart a new lease of life.Every contribution matters. Every share counts. Every life matters.Please share this campaign with your friends, family and business networks. Together, we can multiply our impact and reach more children in need.With heartfelt gratitude,Sudheer MerugumallaFounder & CEO, Noel FoundationHealing Hearts. Empowering Futures.

campaigns.title: Launch Careers of Rural Women       क़ाबिल.कमाऊ.कामयाब
campaigns.description: Sajhe Sapne innovates for young rural women's freedom.Our next big bold bet - shift gender norms in Bundelkhand. Bundelkhand is rich in culture but marked by terrible gender inequality.Join the क़ाबिल कमाऊ कामयाब movement for rural women in Bundelkhand to #LearnEarnExcel.Donate TODAY! (Read on to learn more)About Sajhe Sapne:Sajhe Sapne innovates for young rural women's freedom.We are chasing a big & under-researched question :How to ensure rural women have a real choice of a thriving career after 12th?India has a crisis of not believing in its rural women.Most of the 80M young rural women have no career dreams. Those who do, don’t have a clear path to chase them. 70% are forced into subsistence-based livelihoods.Ecosystem that provides high paying jobs is non-existent for rural women.We are creating a women’s movement that lets rural women dream.Innovations Overview:In the last 4 yrs, our innovations have focused on shifting mindset from "livelihoods" to long-term "career pathways" amongst young rural women.Results Overview:Our small-scale pilots have been a success.Year after year, we have seen young rural women becoming confident professionals instead of teen brides.They are earning more than men around them, delaying marriages, earning steadily & becoming. decision makers in the family.BIG Lessons:Four years of experiments showed us how much innovation is lacking for rural women. The two things that we have discovered as make-break for our work:Make: When a critical mass of young women earn steadily at least for a year, it starts shifting gender norms in that region.Break: Women's freedom can't sustain without collectivising influencers in their life such as family, government & markets.A new impact equation emerged:To test this equation at scale, we want to kickstart the क़ाबिल कमाऊ कामयाब movement in Bundelkhand - a region with troubling gender inequality indicators.The aim is to create a critical mass of rural women in Bundelkhand getting into steady workforce post 12th grade.With the funds in this campaign, we hope to do the following activities: Village Level: Establish at least three centers to test replicability of our model.District Level: Host at least one सामूहिक सपना समेल्लन in two districts to celebrate village clusters & businesses opening doors for rural women.State Level: Improve rural women's participation in government employment schemes such as PM Internship Scheme.If all goes well, we hope to see three key results over the years:% increase of rural women getting into steady workforce after finishing 12th.% increase for villages where women's marriages are delayed at least by 2 yrs% increase for businesses who are actively hiring rural women.These three norms shifts in the system make rural women क़ाबिल कमाऊ कामयाब.As Sajhe Sapne makes this big bold bet, we are counting on you to help us experiment, fail, & discover.Every donation counts. Every shoutout matters.-----------------------------------------------------------To get a glimpse of Sajhe's world, please check our website, instagram & youtube.Or reach out to us, sapnewaalis@gmail.com

campaigns.title: Empowerment of the Blind
campaigns.description:
Visually impaired, consisting of the blind and low vision are one of the most disadvantaged group in the country. Unfortunately India has the highest population of the blind in the world at 150 million. The 2011 Census and other surveys have revealed that the literacy and employment rate of the visually impaired population is at a dismal state when compared to other sections of the population. There is a deep connection between poverty and disability and hence the visually impaired are not in a position to pay for their own education and other rehabilitation services. Only 10% are graduates and more than 72% are unemployed.Visually impaired need reading material in accessible formats like Braille and Audio, support of special educators for school education, assistive technology training and equipment’s and skill building programs to enhance employability. There is a lack of such services in the mainstream. There is a need to sustain and scale up the immensely successful Integrated Education and Technology Training for the Blind programs of NAB Delhi to empower more visually impaired.  
 NAB Delhi will provide its students support for food and accomodation and quality education in mainstream schools. Till the Corona related restrictions are in place these services will be provided at home using online channels or home visits and later at NAB Delhi’s hostel and classrooms in South Delhi. NAB Delhi has been a pioneer in providing ICT training to visually impaired persons of all age groups. We will continue our training programs and scale it up to reach needy persons from all over the country. We will be providing reading material free of cost through our Digital Library and resolution of queries through our Assistive Technology Helpline. The  Centre for Multi-Disabled will provide the much needed special care and vocational training to deafblind and multi-disabled.  
 Every year 250 blind children will receive life-changing quality education in best schools through our support. All their requirements will be met by the organization. More than 300 visually impaired will become digitally literate and receive employability enhancing trainings. 40,000 visually impaired from all over the country will benefit from our Digital Library and Helpline services.100+ deafblind and multi-disabled will get critical care, support and trainings to become independent. Many teachers, NGOs and the mainstream society will benefit from our awareness and capacity building programs.

campaigns.title: Therapeutic Community For Victims of Sex Trafficking
campaigns.description:
Commercial sexual exploitation (CSE) is one of the most disparaging crimes crippling India’s social development and economy and threatening the dignity and security of women and children. In this context, the southern states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are no exception. These states continue to constitute the core destination areas for the victimization of trafficked women and children for economic profiteering at the cost of their human rights. Despite the absence of official statistics on CSE in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, civil society organisation estimates suggest that one out of every four victims rescued from CSE is a child and 60 per cent of all rescued children from CSE are HIV positive. Further, 75 per cent of females in the Telugu region between the ages of 15-35 years are found to be engaged in sex work.[1] Reports in the print and digital news media also indicate that sex trafficking of both vulnerable women and children is progressively on the increase. Given the scale of the issue, the government has not placed due attention and priority on the rescue and rehabilitation of CSE victims in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. In addition, there is a lack of systems and capacity to conduct MEL and research, weak and uncoordinated monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) of existing programs and no investment in empirical research to understand gaps and issues. Rehabilitation of trafficking survivors remains the most persistent challenge within the current legislative framework. Rescued victims require specialised support services to recover from and overcome the years of trauma-induced mental health issues, physical atrocities and social stigma attached to being former sex slaves. In the absence of statutory rehabilitation that ensures complete and sustainable reintegration into society, CSE victims, even if removed temporarily from their immediate environment marked by social, economic, sexual, psychological and physical extremities, are highly likely to end up in the same vicious cycle of sex trafficking, either through the nexus of same perpetrators or new agents who are on the lookout for feeding on their aggravated vulnerabilities for the second time around. On-ground organisations lament that CSE victims who only receive piece-meal assistance and support post-rescue remain uncertain about their future prospects in absence of hope for alternate opportunities to sustain themselves and end up going back to sex slavery. The circumstances surrounding this lack of choice with CSE victims are marked by haplessness and isolation due to lack of specialised support services for destigmatizing their identities and acute availability of comprehensive rehabilitation measures. Given the scale of CSE in both Telugu states, the following issues have emerged:There is no comprehensive protection and rehabilitation policy in place for CSE victims, either in the states or at the national level. Nor there are adequate budgetary allocations in the two states. In fact, Andhra Pradesh does not even have a budget line for CSE rehabilitation facilities and services.  Rescue operations for removing victims of CSE from situations of abuse are ill-conceived and ill-executed due to a lack of comprehensive understanding of the crime and tactical expertise and a lack of industry standards for conducting such raids and rescues.Institutional infrastructure (shelter homes/protective and rehabilitative homes/child care institutions) for rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of CSE is insufficient and severely ill-equipped to address their complex needs for recovery and effective, holistic rehabilitation, whose numbers are advancing with each passing year. As per an article published in the Indian Journal of Gender Studies, there is a lack of comprehensive protection services such as psychological counselling from trained counsellors through the Ujjawala and Swadhar schemes. This issue was further exacerbated in 2014 after the bifurcation of the Telugu region between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana 2014, where most rehabilitation homes fell under Telangana’s territory and Andhra Pradesh was left with close to none. At present, both states have 5 shelter homes each, for women.There is a severe gap in meaningful and relevant data to even gain an understanding of the gaps and barriers in the rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of CSE victims. A study suggests that though there is abundant literature on trafficking worldwide as well as in South Asia, we still do need region-specific and locally-contextualised data that will yield theoretical and empirical insights, and lead to relevant policy interventions. 
 Sex trafficking is a multi-dimensional problem especially with regard to its impact on the lives of the victims. The tormenting experiences of being betrayed, sold and exploited by the people around (largely includes pimps, brothel owners and customers) takes a long-term toll on the victims. This traumatic situation combined with sexually transmitted diseases, chronic depression, suicidal tendencies, alcohol and drug addiction complicates the cycle of rehabilitation. Hence, the process of rehabilitation has to be an interlinked chain of psychological healing, vocational empowerment, economically viable and socially acceptable. In order to address the physical, emotional and psychological brokenness of the sex-trafficked victims, Prajwala formulated a holistic, therapeutic approach to support the rehabilitation process. The overall aim is to help the victims to overcome their trauma by providing them with psychological and coping skills and tools required to regain stability to lead a normal life. Therefore, the rehabilitation in Prajwala is a blend of psychological healing, civic empowerment and social identity. The three-pronged stages of rehabilitation spearheaded by Prajwala include:Psychological Rehabilitation: Trauma Care, Counselling, Psychiatric CareEconomic Rehabilitation: Life-Skills, Employability Training, Education/Livelihood programCivic Rehabilitation: Aadhar Card, Bank Account, Interim Relief, CompensationA therapeutic community as a safe shelter has been established that provides holistic rehabilitation and has been instrumental in the social reintegration support of thousands of victims 
 600 victims of sex trafficking will be supported every year

campaigns.title: Rehabilitation Center for Roadside and Helpless People
campaigns.description:
We observed so many senior citizens in the rural and urban areas; who have children but still struggle for their day-to-day existence. The children are either not in the same city or are not in a position to care for their parents. He wants to be able to cater to these senior citizens, providing a place of residence that they can call ‘Home’, eliminating the sense of abandonment and instilling a sense of belonging in its place. As a country, and as individuals we have a moral and ethical obligation to ensure that these people are well looked after and cared for. Just like all of us, they too deserve love and nurturing! 
 Activities 1.     Selection of Residents: Meet/interview the elderly, at the road site, near the temple under the bridge, taking permission from the police and enrolling in Ashram.2.     Doing all pathology tests as per need and suggested by Doctor.3.     Daily/Activities Routine: Prepare and share the daily plan with each resident and staff as part of the Orientation – this should include details of daily routine, access to different facilities, food, medical facilities, etc.4.     Health & Nutrition: the nutritionist will prepare a meal plan based on the resident’s needs and instruct/train the kitchen staff, and also ensure adherence to the plan. The nutritionist will work closely with the kitchen staff to plan, and ensure adherence to meal plans and any specific dietary requirements. 5.     Healthcare & Medical: Doctors and nurses will ensure that all residents adhere to their medical specifications and also regular check-ups as per the needs of each resident. 6.     Recreation Plan: The OAH will develop activities daily that not only focus on the health of residents but also the recreational activities so that their mental health is in check and they are occupied with various activities that will help them boost their stay and make them feel like they are at ‘HOME’ – celebrating special days, festivals, cultural events, activities and events focussed on spiritual development, games, and fun, 7.     Agriculture activity:- Identifying people who are physically fit and have an interest in working in the agriculture field. Local people have been given agricultural filed to cultivate the land. Using agriculture products for Ashram. 8.     Cleanliness drive: - Once a quarter we are doing cleanliness drives at the railway station, Near Smashan Bhumu, and the school. Taking participation of local volunteers. 9.     CARE (Committed Action For Relief and Education):- Involving CARE students to Identify people at the Road site, Alone elderly people at home, and various activities of JAS. 10. Providing daily Lunch to alone Elderly people in Villages: - We are Identifying needy and alone elderly people in villages and starting lunch box services. As no one has the capacity to provide food to them on a daily basis. Since its inception, JAS has organized many activities such as providing ration, and health treatment to road site people. Also, during the winter season team provided blankets at midnight to needy people who were staying under a bridge or on the road. The team did regular outreach at the roadside to Identify destitute people for providing them with services. Conducted awareness sessions in schools and colleges to create awareness about Important of elderly people.•       After continuous regular follow-up and with the staff’s efforts. We rehabilitated 135 people in their own homes and reunited them with their families.•       Done rehabilitation of 766 destitute at JAS Ashram till today at various Ashrams•     Provided support to 70 people with services like grains, Food, health treatment, and clothes at the roadside and under the bridge during this period at midnight.   
 To establish a well-managed, community participated, and safe Old Aged Home.Provide primary medical, and day-to-day welfare assistance - maintaining good health is the key issue for older people. In providing appropriate treatment, medication, and overall health care services, older people can remain active, which will not only address their self-respect and dignity but also reduces their dependency and increases their productive life.Instill a feeling of ‘belonging,’ through recreational activities, and awareness campaigns, giving them ‘hope’ for the future and a sense of purpose. To provide access to fellowship activities, recreational facilities, mental support, social affairs, and spiritual formation. To act as a centre where the knowledge and experiences of the senior citizens is utilized in a constructive manner to contribute more meaningfully to both, the residents and society.
